parallel.requirements: Recognized the required pure JavaScript ESM implementation, .mjs files, local imports, manual argument parsing, AES-ECB behavior, Python bytes repr formatting, and prohibition on external packages and node:crypto Cipher APIs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent probed reference behavior, then assigned four subagents to non-overlapping modules: AES tables/core, ECB plus pybytes, argparse, and test15 entry point. The parent retained final integration and verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote root-level /output modules. AES core supported AES-128/192/256 block operations; ECB and pybytes were separate modules; argparse exported parseArgs(argv, prog); the entry child initially called parseArgs(prog, argv, spec).
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After the swarm returned, the parent inspected the handoff, noticed the parseArgs signature mismatch, edited /output/test15.mjs to call parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2), prog), and delivered six root-level .mjs files.
parallel.verification: Children ran scoped tests, and the parent ran end-to-end comparisons for four samples, checked equals-form and error cases, and ran 20 randomized differential tests against the executable.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluator still marked the solution failed at 6/29 despite the parent-visible sample and fuzz checks; the visible coordination defect was repaired, so the remaining failures are not proven to be caused by that defect.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure Node.js ESM, local module, CLI alignment, AES-ECB, bytes repr, no npm, and no node:crypto Cipher requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the entire port from probing through implementation, writing AES tables/core, ECB, pybytes, argparse, and entry point sequentially without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote a /output/test15.mjs entry point and /output/lib modules, fixed its initial AES ShiftRows mistake by rewriting the core file, and used a local parser and bytes repr helper.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor owned all files, parser and entry-point integration happened in the same local flow; the artifact validation later listed test15.mjs and lib module files.
serial.verification: The serial actor compared selected sample cases to the executable, corrected a shell delimiter mistake in its test harness, checked edge cases, and ran 30 randomized fuzz comparisons.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluator also marked this solution failed at 6/29, so the visible verification did not cover the hidden official failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel preserved the task prompt requirements in child briefs: pure Node.js ESM, .mjs files, local imports, manual argv parsing, AES-ECB, Python bytes repr, and no external dependencies.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the identical prompt and recognized the same command-line, output-format, ESM, module-layout, and dependency constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both missed or under-tested whatever hidden obligations caused the same official 6/29 failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into four subagents with module-level ownership and a parent integration role.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation or subagents and kept implementation, integration, testing, and closure in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained module-level concurrency but introduced an inter-agent API boundary; serial avoided that boundary through single-actor ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The argparse child implemented parseArgs(argv, prog), while the entry-point child guessed parseArgs(prog, argv, spec) and explicitly flagged the uncertainty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote the parser and entry point in one trajectory, so the parser call convention stayed local rather than crossing a child boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete cross-agent interface mismatch that required a parent repair; serial did not split that API contract across actors.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced root-level aes_tables.mjs, aes_core.mjs, ecb_mode.mjs, pybytes.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test15.mjs from separate child implementations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced test15.mjs plus lib/aes-tables.mjs, lib/aes-core.mjs, lib/ecb.mjs, lib/pybytes.mjs, and lib/argparse.mjs from a single implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file layout and authorship differed, but both created an artifact accepted for evaluation and both remained short of hidden official acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned through the AgentSwarm aggregate, after which the parent inspected them and took follow-up integration action.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; the same actor proceeded from writes through verification and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an explicit child-result join and post-handoff repair step; serial had no retrievable child results to join or lose.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct root-level files into shared /output; the parent later edited the entry deliverable to align it with argparse.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all modules itself, first under /output/lib and then the entry point that imported those local modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared workspace had a repaired cross-file API integration problem; serial integration was sequential and local to one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child scoped tests, four sample comparisons, equals and error checks, then 20 randomized differential tests before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample comparisons, corrected a shell harness delimiter issue, checked edge cases, then ran 30 randomized fuzz comparisons.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both performed visible differential verification but neither visible test plan matched the official hidden suite closely enough to pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout, used four subagents, 32 tool calls, and more total tokens before delivering a completed final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout, used no subagents, 14 tool calls, and fewer total tokens before delivering a completed final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more coordination overhead but no direct timeout or cancellation; the official outcome remained the same as serial.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status.json evaluations show both modes failed with 6 of 29 samples passed, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The parallel run's distinctive coordination event was a missing parser-entry interface contract that produced an unplanned repair, while the serial run's visible defects and fixes were ordinary local implementation work. Because both final artifacts reached the evaluator and received the same official score, the retained coordination pattern is an adverse parallel process event rather than an evidenced cause of an outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Parallel split parser and entry-point ownership and had to repair the parseArgs signature mismatch after the swarm returned.
Parallel nevertheless completed visible sample and randomized differential verification before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial kept parser and entry-point ownership local to one actor and avoided that cross-agent API mismatch.
Serial also completed visible sample, edge, and fuzz verification but still failed the official hidden suite.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial initially wrote a flawed AES core section and rewrote it locally; this is an ordinary coding defect, not a coordination pattern.
The two artifacts used different file layouts, root-level modules in parallel and lib modules in serial, but artifact validation accepted both layouts.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official evaluator results are visible in the mounted pair; detailed hidden failing cases are not present.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel adverse but not outcome differential
